Frontend: /contributors wall renders 2 seeded cards; wall-filter-input filters real-time (typed 'veg' → 1 card veggie_wizard), wall-filter-clear resets, wall-filter-no-results empty state with 'No contributors matching “X”.' text; wall-recover-<nick> visible only when nickname NOT in localStorage.owned_nicknames (verified by seeding + reload); recovery-dialog opens with recovery-send-code button + amber warning on step 1; WallShareDialog shows all 4 theme chips (mint/rose/midnight/sunset), clicking sunset updates canvas gradient background + nickname gradient (visual confirmed via screenshot), stores 'sunset' in localStorage['irr.wall_share_theme'], persists across dialog reopen (sunset chip has ring-2 selected state on reopen); format toggle still works with theme applied (canvas 1080×1080 square ↔ 1200×630 landscape).
critical_code_review_comments: Recovery upsert on nickname_recoveries keys on {nickname} only — no unique index. Concurrent requests overwrite each other's code (last-write-wins). That's actually desirable here (invalidates prior codes), but should be documented since it means only the LATEST code works after multiple requests.

verify_nickname_recovery compares nickname path param with payload.nickname via _sanitize_nickname — good defense-in-depth. But it does not verify payload.new_email is different from the current owner; user could 'transfer' to same email, which is a no-op but still consumes the single-use code. Low priority.

_mask_email format 'a***@***.com' hides the domain name completely (only TLD shown). Compared to typical 'a***@d***.com' pattern (per the task description), this is actually MORE conservative — safer against enumeration. Aligns with the request body's 'a***@***.com' example so this is correct.

NicknameRecoveryDialog calls setTimeout(window.location.reload, 500) on success. On slow networks the toast may not render before reload wipes it. Consider showing a persistent success state before reload, or drop the reload and trigger a re-fetch prop instead. Minor UX polish.

Recovery endpoint does not rate-limit: an attacker could brute-force 6-digit codes at ~10 req/s (1M / 10 = ~28h expected). Combined with 30-min TTL that's ~1/56 chance per code lifetime — non-trivial. Consider adding lockout after N failed verifies per nickname, or throttling per-IP. HIGH-value future work but not blocking.
Nickname recovery doc stores plaintext code. If DB is exfiltrated, active codes are usable for their 30-min window. Consider hashing (bcrypt/sha256) at rest. Medium priority.
WallShareDialog THEMES palette localStorage read on mount uses THEMES.find with a fallback to THEMES[0] — safe even if stored value is stale/invalid. Good.
ContributorWall filteredContributors useMemo re-runs on every keystroke; for 2-500 contributors this is trivial. No debouncing needed at this scale.
